text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a sudden drop in prefix cache hit-rate for chat workloads after last night's kernel-selection tweak. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/priming/kv-hitrate (look at chat-rag split)
maria: ugh, how big is the drop? numbers?
alex: ~18% -> ~6% for chat (p50 request mix), RAG barely changes (stays ~22%). overall token cost +12% for chat-heavy tenants.
jin: did we change key normalization or key format in that deploy? sounds like key mismatch
alex: no explicit key format changes. The PR (https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/492) changed kernel selection heuristics and bumped a tiny reordering in the batching path. suspect the prefix hash includes a KV cache metadata field that might be reordered.
sean: Can you paste the cache key generation snippet? small differences can explode cardinality.
alex: sure — sample log from canary:

```
cache_key=v1|model=gptx-7b|mode=chat|tenant=acme|prefix_sha=9f3a2b|kv_meta={"seg":5,"order":1}
```

and another one for similar request (post-change):

```
cache_key=v1|model=gptx-7b|mode=chat|tenant=acme|prefix_sha=9f3a2b|kv_meta={"order":1,"seg":5}
```
maria: yep that's it. kv_meta ordering not deterministic -> unique keys for same prefix. RAG probably forms keys differently (uses doc_id canonicalization) so unaffected.
jin: where was kv_meta assembled? I thought we stringify a map directly in runtime/batching -> cache_key_builder
alex: PR switched to using the json serializer from the kernel utils (faster) which doesn't guarantee stable key ordering. previously we used OrderedMap in go->stable stringifier in the runtime.
sean: ok that's a regression in key stability. We should roll back that part or canonicalize before hashing. Quick mitigation: strip kv_meta from the key for chat workloads (low impact) until we fix.
maria: +1 for strip. Also need to add unit test that asserts stable key output across N shuffles.
alex: I've queued a hotfix (internal PR 497) that normalizes kv_meta (sorted keys) and adds tests. Running canary now.
perf-bot: Canary deploy 1908765460 -> runtime/serve:v2026.03.18-hotfix-497 started
alex: initial canary metrics: chat hit-rate back up to ~17% within 10m. still watching for tail cases.
jin: good. while we're here, can we add a fast path in kernel selector that avoids touching kv_meta for pure completion flows? we saw some perf regressions when kernel selection queries metadata for every request.
maria: kernel selector should be cheap — but agreed, avoid doing expensive JSON ops in hot path. maybe memoize per-model-config.
sean: also check batching heuristics. The tweak that reordered the batch path combined kernel selection + batching decisions; if key stability fix removes churn but batching still reorders, we might see transient cold misses.
alex: noted. I profiled the fast-path: the JSON stringify added ~120ns/request but the real pain was that miss rates cause recompute of KV cache fill which is heavier.
jin: do we have a reproducible workload to run locally? a chat-heavy driver with ~70% prefix reuse.
alex: yes — script: tools/perf/drivers/chat_warmup.py --seed 42 --reuse 0.7

```
# quick repro
python tools/perf/drivers/chat_warmup.py --seed 42 --reuse 0.7 --profile=kv
```
maria: let's add that to CI perf and gate the kernel selector change behind a canary + perf check in the future.
sean: agreed. Also add a histogram of per-prefix cardinality to the console (per-tenant) so support can see when keys blow up.
alex: logged follow-ups: PATCH-1 (hotfix merge), PATCH-2 (memoize kernel selector + avoid json op), PATCH-3 (metrics + CI test). I'll link PRs once open.
perf-bot: Canary deploy succeeded on 3/3 hosts at 1908765488
alex: final note — this is an example of how small changes in servicer-local serialization can cascade. We'll add an architectural doc section about canonicalization and hot-path invariants.
maria: thanks for catching. :tada:
jin: nice catch. I'll review 497 now.
sean: if anyone sees odd per-tenant costs over next 24h, ping here and we'll triage.
deploy-bot: Rolling restart scheduled for runtime/serve to complete hotfix rollout (ETA 3m)"
